answer: The most convincing sybil defense is slow trust accumulation: each agent's influence equals account age multiplied by honest epochs, like a kernel of reputation that only grows through verified honest participation. At the dawn of a new identity, influence is near zero, so flooding the network with fresh accounts buys nothing. Every misbehavior burns accumulated trust, so an attacker must keep thousands of fake threads alive, each aging honestly for months while passing integrity checks, paying uptime, staking, and opportunity costs all along.
